scope: Theorem 4.1 (Frame coefficient bound) of the manuscript “Rational homology and Quillen's conjecture” (preprints/Rational-homology-and-Quillens-conjecture-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 310 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 62d7903055f1b292), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 15. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let W have dimension h ≥ 2 and one of the four structures above, and suppose that W admits an allowed frame. The space Z(W) ⊆ ⨁ D∈F(W) VD consists of cycles of degree h − 2, each supported on full flags ending at sign groups of rank h − 1. Moreover, dim Z(W) ≥ Fh |F(W)|(h − 1)!. (11) The following choices of Fh are valid for each individual isometry type of W. (i) In the no-form case over Fu, and in the hermitian case over Fu2 , set ρ = 1 u(u + 1) and ρ = 1 u(u − 1) , respectively, y = 1 + √ 1 − 4ρ 2 . For u ≥ 5 one may take Fh = yh + (1 − y)h ≥ (17/25)h. (ii) For a symmetric space over Fu, with both line types allowed and u ≥ 5 odd, put x = 1 + √ 1 − 4u/(u2 − 1) 2 . One may take Fh = xh + (1 − x)h − 12|h 2(u2 − 1)−h/2 ≥ (17/25)h . (12) In particular F3 ≥ 3/8. (iii) For a symmetric space over Fu with one fixed line type, where u ≥ 7 is odd, write χ for the quadratic character of F× u and set ρ = 2 u − χ(−1) , y = 1 + √ 1 − 4ρ 2 . One may take Fh = yh + (1 − y)h > 0. The same statements hold for any realization by projective sign subgroups in which coarsened decompositions give the indicated subgroup flags and the complete flags ending at the full frames remain distinct.
